text: The dynamic-programming algorithm that finds the optimal LOCAL alignment between two sequences (as opposed to Needleman-Wunsch's global alignment) is called the ___ algorithm.
explanation: The Smith-Waterman algorithm (1981) formulates local sequence alignment as a dynamic programming problem, finding the best-matching subsequence rather than aligning entire sequences end to end. Needleman-Wunsch (1970), by contrast, is the earlier dynamic-programming algorithm for global alignment; the local/global distinction is foundational to modern search tools such as BLAST.
